# Study scope

The submitted report uses daily token prices, returns, trading volume and
Bitcoin, Ethereum and Chiliz benchmarks. It does not use Google Trends or a
financial-stress index. The default R workflow follows its completed Phase 3
scope while retaining the original methodology paper's R detection packages.
The original repository and optional additional paper analyses remain included.

The primary sample ends on 30 June 2026, with an extension through 19 September
2026. Each cutoff is estimated independently. All 20 fan tokens and all three
benchmarks retain their own first valid trading dates. Input prices are adjusted
daily USD closes on a UTC calendar, with no forward-filling or winsorization.

The methodology chapter and completed Phase 3 use different specifications.
The latter uses zero-lag regressions, approximate reference thresholds, a 30-day
dating rule and a local-ADF Bayesian model. The default follows those choices;
it does not claim the proposed bootstrap or hierarchical models were fitted.
See `../Working-paper/Report-alignment.txt` for the comparison.

# Libraries and execution

The core detection methods use the paper's `exuber` 1.1.0 and `cpm` 2.3 packages.
The Bayesian local-ADF extension is implemented in base R. JSON parsing uses
`jsonlite`; file verification uses `digest`. No Python process is invoked.

```{r regenerate, eval=params$regenerate}
source("run_all.R")
```

The default render displays included outputs. Set `regenerate=TRUE` to execute
the complete analysis while knitting, or run `Rscript run_all.R` first.

# Data processing

`R/01_process_data.R` reconstructs daily data from all archived provider JSON
responses, checks dates and duplicate prices, flags invalid observations and
calculates adjacent-day log returns and 30-day volatility. The daily analysis
snapshots are saved as `Processed-data/daily_panel_2026-06-30.csv` and
`Processed-data/daily_panel_2026-09-19.csv`. Monthly/weekly datasets remain
available for optional paper extensions and are not inputs to this daily run.

```{r sample}
knitr::kable(read_table(file.path(report_dir, "sample_comparison.csv")))
```

# Recursive detection and episode dating

`exuber::radf()` is applied to daily log adjusted prices with an intercept and
zero lagged differences. Its minimum-window argument counts regression rows;
the reported PSY window counts price observations, so an explicit one-row
conversion preserves the submitted estimation windows.

The original reference-table interpolation/extrapolation and SADF-based endpoint
approximation are retained for comparison with Phase 3. These outputs are
nominal reference classifications, not bootstrap p-values or matched BSADF
simulated critical values. At least 30 consecutive daily exceedances are
required for a retained interval. A statistical interval can accompany a price
decline, so its price change is reported explicitly.

```{r recursive-statistics}
t <- read_table(file.path(report_dir, "psy_test_summary.csv"))
knitr::kable(t[t$asset_type == "fan_token", c("cutoff_date", "symbol", "observations", "sadf_statistic", "gsadf_statistic", "gsadf_cv_95", "gsadf_reject_95", "longest95_run")], digits = 4)
```

```{r persistent-intervals}
knitr::kable(read_table(file.path(report_dir, "psy_persistent_intervals.csv")), digits = 4)
```

# Sequential distribution changes

The methodology paper's actual `cpm::processStream()` Kolmogorov-Smirnov model
is applied to daily log returns. Startup uses 20% of the valid return sample,
rounded upward, with a minimum of 30 observations. ARL0 is 500, with 1000 as a
sensitivity check. Estimated change dates and subsequent detection dates are
exported separately.

This preserves the paper's nonparametric sequential method. The submitted
Phase 3 instead used penalized segmentation of mean and log squared returns.
Their change counts differ; the submitted 76.8% volatility-shift result is not
recomputed or attributed to KS-CPM.

```{r ks-changes}
knitr::kable(read_table(file.path(report_dir, "ks_cpm_change_points.csv")))
```

# Bayesian diagnostics and benchmark comparisons

The local-ADF model actually used in Phase 3 is ported to base R: normal
coefficient priors, slope-prior standard deviation 0.5, standardized innovation
variance fixed at one and expected run length 365 days. It exports reset and
positive-slope probabilities. Full-sample scaling is retrospective within each
cutoff. It is distinct from both the paper's BSTS forecasts and the methodology
chapter's proposed normal-inverse-gamma return model.

Daily return correlations compare every fan token against BTC, ETH and CHZ.
They describe co-movement and do not establish causality.

```{r benchmark-comparisons}
knitr::kable(read_table(file.path(report_dir, "benchmark_return_correlations.csv")), digits = 4)
```

```{r daily-diagnostics, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(list.files(report_figure_dir, pattern = "[.]png$", full.names = TRUE))
```

# Results and verification

```{r generated-summary, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("```text\n", paste(readLines(file.path(report_dir, "RESULTS.txt")), collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

Validation compares the R recursive statistics, original sample counts,
persistent intervals and local-ADF probabilities against the archived outputs
underlying the submission. KS-CPM is checked as its own model and is not forced
to reproduce penalized-segmentation counts. Raw inputs and the submitted Word
document are retained unchanged.

```{r method-scope}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/method_status.csv"))
```

# Optional original paper extensions

`run_paper_extensions.R` and `Paper-extensions.Rmd` preserve the earlier monthly
and weekly paper profile, ARIMA/BSTS forecasting and benchmark Johansen/VECM.
Those results remain separate from this submitted-report analysis. Google
Trends, sentiment density analysis and financial-stress propagation belong to
additional original-paper sections; they are outside this project's submitted
empirical scope. The complete original R source is in `../Original-paper/`.
